description: Somos un equipo de Cajamarca, Perú, que desarrolla una herramienta de monitoreo de salud para astronautas en misiones de larga duración. Usa análisis de datos en tiempo real y machine learning para vigilar signos vitales, detectar alertas tempranas y mostrar paneles claros que ayuden a la tripulación y al control de misión a actuar rápido.
summary: EKEKO is an experimental predictive intelligence system designed for biomedical monitoring and anticipation of medical emergencies during Extravehicular Activities (EVA) in space missions. The system ingests multimodal telemetry from spacesuit sensors, calculates deviations from each astronaut's individual physiological baseline, and predicts the probability of a medical event occurring with a 30-minute anticipation window in its initial MVP version, generating graduated alerts with physiological explanation, causal hypothesis, and recommended actions.
details:
EKEKO Health Monitoring System

Complementary Documentation: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/13rXvk2iNeual1qDQEB6TswUkiAdyVy7Z?usp=sharing

What does it do / How does it work?

  • Ingests multimodal telemetry from spacesuit sensors (heart rate, SpO₂, respiratory rate, core/skin temp, EEG, EMG, radiation)
  • Calculates individual physiological baselines per astronaut/session (30-min window)
  • Predicts medical event probability 30 minutes in advance using AI
  • Generates graduated alerts (watch/alert/critical) with deviated variables, causal hypothesis, and recommended actions
  • 7-stage pipeline: Sensors → Telemetry/Events capture → PostgreSQL (12 tables) → Baseline calc → AI prediction → Alert generation → Medical control panel

Benefits:

  • Technological: Heterogeneous biomedical telemetry integrated in audited PostgreSQL (3NF) with full traceability
  • Human safety: 15-30 min earlier response to hypoxia, hyperthermia, radiation exposure
  • Operational: Reduces alert fatigue (target ≤1 false alarm/session at alert level)
  • Explainability: Full chain — detect, classify, explain deviations, hypothesize cause, recommend action, escalate, learn

Intended Impact:

  • Medical safety/autonomy for astronauts during EVAs
  • Decision support for flight surgeons (executive summaries with action windows)
  • Mission control visibility + false alarm control
  • Research dataset with labeled events, metrics, feature importance

Tools/Languages/Hardware/Software:

  • Languages: Python (backend), React (frontend), SQL
  • Database: PostgreSQL (ENUM, UNIQUE, CHECK, JSONB)
  • Modeling: ER diagrams, UML, conceptual design tools
  • Sensors modeled: Pulse oximeter, 2-channel frontal EEG, surface EMG, radiation dosimeter

Team Considerations:

  • Temporal leakage prevention (exclude active-event records from training)
  • Sensor observability gaps (indirect proxy measurements, no invasive diagnostics)
  • Clinical disclaimer: doesn't replace medical judgment
  • Normalization tradeoffs (JSONB conditional 1NF, transitive dependency in ALERTS)
  • Space environment constraints: limited sensors, no hospital equipment, irreversible events in minutes
